Triage (first touch): **`pm:queue` + `domain:ui`**.

Landing: `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx` — the `ComponentRegistry.register('dashboard', …)` call that publishes three inputs while `DashboardRenderer` honours seven. `packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts` is the reference surface, not the fix site.

Graded `pm:queue` rather than `finding`: the body names the landing call, and the remedy is the one already shipped twice for this exact class (#4668 / #5091) — publish the inputs the renderer reads. No open question.

objectui three-stream split (maintainer 2026-08-21). Routed via the maintainer direct-dispatch channel, this session, verbatim: 「objectui 有 79 张卡在车道视图之外（占该仓 35%），你帮我分批处理」 · 「继续 批 2 批 3」. PM session `session_0124Qg8rLvpXnQDwCmpKUmaJ`. Not a Routine triage fire — the triage seat may re-grade.

Taken on the triage grading's own reasoning: the body names the landing call and the remedy is the one already shipped twice for this class (#4668 / #5091), so there is no open question to route back.

⚠️ The one thing that is **not** mechanical, restated for the dev: #5091 settled that some honoured keys are deliberately **non-author** surface, decided per key — so this is not "declare all seven". Each honoured key gets a decision, and the deliberate exclusions get pinned the way `gridNonAuthorKeys.test.tsx` pins them, rather than being left as a silent gap that reads identically to an oversight. `widgets` is the floor (every example in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` authors it, and #5709's unconsumed-options warning already descends into it).

⛔ `packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts` is the reference surface, not the fix site.

**PM ruling on the open question — option B: `name` is NOT an author input on the inline `dashboard` node.** `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EuPCi56cnGyykygi3z9w4m`.

I am ruling B, but on a stronger ground than the report's balance-of-axes, and the difference matters for the pin's wording.

## The shipped heuristic does not fire here — this is not a close call

The line is *"spec accepts + renderer reads ⇒ declare"*. The report reads the first clause as satisfied because "the spec ACCEPTS `name`". But it accepts it **on the document form**, where it is *required* — not on the inline node. The shape the spec is accepting `name` on is not the shape this registration publishes inputs for.

So the premise of the heuristic is not met, and B wins without needing the four axes at all. `title` and `aria` were excluded because the spec **rejects** them; `name` is excluded because the spec's acceptance is **about a different shape**. Those are two different exclusion reasons and the pin should say which one it is — a future reader who sees `name` excluded next to `title` will otherwise assume "spec rejects it" and be wrong.

## The axis that would have decided it anyway

Publishing `name` as an inline input would teach authors — human and, more to the point, AI — to fabricate a dashboard identity inline. Per the report's own measurement, that identity keys `dashboards.{name}.*` translation lookups, so a fabricated one resolves **nothing** and fails silently. That is a **newly manufactured silently-inert key**: precisely the defect class this card exists to remove. Curing seven instances while minting an eighth is not a trade worth making.

## Carry the cost forward honestly

The report names it and it must survive into the code: this pin **cannot** use the "spec rejects by name" leg, because the spec does accept `name`. It rests on **producer evidence alone** — `DashboardView` / the document loader hands the loaded document to the renderer. That makes it a weaker pin than the `title` / `aria` ones, and the docblock should say so, so nobody later reads its silence as the same strength of guarantee. ⛔ Do not paper over that by asserting a spec rejection that does not exist.

Concretely: replace the "pending (not ruled)" marker in the registration comment and the pin test docblock with this ruling, stating (a) that the spec accepts `name` on the **document** form only, (b) that the read stays untouched, and (c) that the pin's evidence is the producer, not a spec verdict.

## On the rest of the card

The per-key work is right. Declaring seven and pinning two exclusions `gridNonAuthorKeys`-style is exactly the #5091 line, and ⛔ the `schema.title || schema.label` read correctly stays while `title` leaves the published surface — advertised and honoured are different questions, and the render leg pins that.

The measured correction to the issue body is the more valuable half and is accepted: the body implies `aria` is a "renderer honours it" key, and the measurement found **zero `schema.aria` read sites in this package**, so there is no "still reads it" leg for it at all. Recording that rather than inheriting the body's framing is the right instinct — and #5830 (the `DashboardComponentSchema.aria` declaration in `@object-ui/types`, under a stale "Aligned with `@objectstack/spec` AriaPropsSchema" comment) is the correct place for the residue, filed unassigned for triage rather than folded in.
